cases.title: Check the inclusive compatibility edges

scope.reference: G-02 module graph and lifecycle on the reference modular monolith, with PostgreSQL and filesystem providers. Trust qualification is supplied by AC-031.

preconditions: A declares support for B versions from 2.0.0 through 2.2.0 inclusive; equivalent fixtures exist at 1.9.9 and 2.2.1.
steps: Compose each of B 1.9.9, 2.0.0, 2.2.0 and 2.2.1 with A, keeping runtime and provider pins fixed.
expectedOutcome: Only 2.0.0 and 2.2.0 satisfy the declared range; each rejected version identifies the same unsatisfied constraint.
evidence: Four resolved-selection reports and the declared compatibility range.

cases.title: Distinguish aliases from additional sites

scope.website: W module composition on one tenant, site and culture; installed Razor renderers, PostgreSQL and filesystem Files only.

preconditions: One site and one culture are configured; two alias bindings have already been qualified by AC-004 and AC-031.
steps: Compose once with no aliases and once with both qualified aliases.
Request a second independent site while retaining the same module set.
expectedOutcome: Both alias selections still describe exactly one site and remain within W.
The second-site selection is rejected as outside W.
evidence: Resolved site counts and capability reports for the three selections.

cases.title: Reject missing, cyclic and incompatible dependencies

scope.reference: G-02 module graph and lifecycle on the reference modular monolith, with PostgreSQL and filesystem providers. Trust qualification is supplied by AC-031.

preconditions: Retain the valid A-to-B-to-C graph and its provider inventory as the control fixture.
steps: Independently remove C, add C-to-A, and replace B with a version outside A's declared range.
Attempt activation for each graph and inspect module state.
expectedOutcome: Each graph is refused before activation; diagnostics name respectively the absent C, complete cycle, and incompatible B constraint.
No module is reported active for the rejected selection.
evidence: Three input graphs, dependency diagnostics and before/after activation inventories.

cases.title: Reject website composition mismatches

scope.website: W module composition on one tenant, site and culture; installed Razor renderers, PostgreSQL and filesystem Files only.

preconditions: Start with a valid W composition and retain a copy for each independent mutation.
steps: Select an incompatible persistence provider; separately remove the required page renderer.
Separately select a second site, a second culture, search, newsletters, GraphQL or commerce; attempt activation for every variant.
expectedOutcome: Every variant fails capability validation before activation with the unsupported selection or missing dependency named.
The valid W composition remains the comparison baseline.
evidence: Mutation matrix, capability diagnostics and activation-state observations.

cases.title: Activate a valid dependency graph

scope.reference: G-02 module graph and lifecycle on the reference modular monolith, with PostgreSQL and filesystem providers. Trust qualification is supplied by AC-031.

preconditions: Module A depends on B; B depends on C; C has no dependencies. All three declare compatible runtime and provider versions.
steps: Compose A, B and C in reverse discovery order.
Start the application and inspect initialization, readiness and shutdown order.
expectedOutcome: Dependencies initialize before dependents, each once; all selected modules become ready.
Shutdown reverses the declared dependency order and completes the recorded lifecycle.
evidence: Resolved graph and version inventory.
Ordered lifecycle trace and readiness observations on host and container.

cases.title: Compose the declared website capability set

scope.website: W module composition on one tenant, site and culture; installed Razor renderers, PostgreSQL and filesystem Files only.

preconditions: The W capability map supplies the selected modules; the page layout, page template and used block renderer versions are installed.
steps: Resolve the module and renderer inventory with the W tuple.
Start the single-host container and inspect its capability report.
expectedOutcome: Every included dependency resolves and the report names the W subset and exact selected versions.
No undeclared capability is inferred from shared modules.
evidence: Composition input, resolved module/renderer graph and runtime capability report.

cases.title: Recover an interrupted module initialization

scope.reference: G-02 module graph and lifecycle on the reference modular monolith, with PostgreSQL and filesystem providers. Trust qualification is supplied by AC-031.

preconditions: C initializes successfully; B has a fault injected after initialization starts but before readiness. A has not started.
steps: Start the graph and trigger the B fault.
Inspect completed cleanup, remove the fault and restart with the identical module selection.
expectedOutcome: The first start reports B failed and A unavailable; cleanup identifies every initialized component.
The second start reaches readiness without duplicate initialization effects or an active remnant from the failed start.
evidence: Failed and recovered lifecycle traces, cleanup inventory and durable initialization-effect counts.

cases.title: Retry composition after restoring a renderer

scope.website: W module composition on one tenant, site and culture; installed Razor renderers, PostgreSQL and filesystem Files only.

preconditions: The page template dependency is absent; the site has a previously usable compatible composition.
steps: Attempt to activate the incomplete selection.
Restore the exact declared renderer version through deployment configuration and repeat preflight and activation.
expectedOutcome: The failed selection never becomes active.
Revalidation resolves the restored renderer and activates the complete selection once.
evidence: Missing-renderer diagnostic, corrected dependency inventory and activation trace.

cases.title: Observe ambient and independent transaction boundaries

scope.reference: G-02 PostgreSQL/EF Core persistence, non-security soft-delete filtering, direct SQL, transactions, concurrency and migrations. Tenant filtering depends on AC-004.

preconditions: The adapter advertises joined, new and suppressed unit-of-work modes for one PostgreSQL database. The suppressed fixture uses an autocommitted direct write on an independent connection; each run uses separate outer and inner rows.
steps: For each mode write the outer row and the inner row, complete the inner scope, then roll back the outer scope.
Inspect committed rows using another connection.
expectedOutcome: The outer row is absent after rollback in all three runs; joined mode also leaves no inner row.
The completed new transaction and suppressed autocommitted write each retain their inner row. No result implies atomicity across databases.
evidence: Declared mode contract, transaction identifiers, completion callbacks and resulting row sets.

cases.title: Check state at the commit boundary

scope.website: W PostgreSQL transactions and optimistic concurrency for content and contact state, with migration recovery on the single database.

preconditions: A contact-1 submission writes its durable request and email intent in one transaction; the connection can be interrupted at controlled points.
steps: Run once with interruption immediately before commit and once immediately after database commit but before the caller receives success.
Inspect the request and intent using a fresh connection.
expectedOutcome: The precommit run retains neither authoritative item.
The postcommit run retains both; a client timeout does not change the recorded database outcome.
evidence: Fault timing, committed transaction identity and request/outbox counts for each run.

cases.title: Reject stale writes and roll back a failed transaction

scope.reference: G-02 PostgreSQL/EF Core persistence, non-security soft-delete filtering, direct SQL, transactions, concurrency and migrations. Tenant filtering depends on AC-004.

preconditions: Two editors have item-1 at version 5; a unit of work can update item-1 and insert item-4.
steps: Save editor A's change and then submit editor B's original version.
In a fresh unit of work change item-1, then inject an insert failure before commit.
expectedOutcome: The stale save reports a concurrency conflict and preserves A's value.
The failed unit of work persists neither change and reports rolled back or failed, never committed.
evidence: Versioned requests, conflict response, fault point and independent database reads after both attempts.

cases.title: Preserve the winner of concurrent website edits

scope.website: W PostgreSQL transactions and optimistic concurrency for content and contact state, with migration recovery on the single database.

preconditions: Two Admin sessions read article-1 at the same version; both are prequalified for the operation.
steps: Save title First from one session.
Submit title Second with the stale token from the other session.
Force an outbox insert failure in a separate new save.
expectedOutcome: The stale write returns a typed conflict and does not replace First.
The separately failed save commits neither the proposed revision nor its outbox intent.
evidence: Requests and error responses, before/after revision hashes and database transaction outcomes.

cases.title: Commit a unit of work and apply soft-delete filters

scope.reference: G-02 PostgreSQL/EF Core persistence, non-security soft-delete filtering, direct SQL, transactions, concurrency and migrations. Tenant filtering depends on AC-004.

preconditions: PostgreSQL contains active rows item-1 and item-2 plus soft-deleted item-3 in the prequalified context. A declared direct-SQL access path uses the same application filter contract.
steps: Read through EF Core and the declared direct-SQL path.
In one unit of work update item-1 and create item-4; commit and reread through a new connection.
expectedOutcome: Both reads return item-1 and item-2 and omit item-3.
The new connection sees both committed changes; the completion callback reports committed once.
evidence: Provider/version inventory, query results, transaction trace and completion callback record.

cases.title: Commit a draft and its durable event intent together

scope.website: W PostgreSQL transactions and optimistic concurrency for content and contact state, with migration recovery on the single database.

preconditions: article-1 is at revision-1 in PostgreSQL; its save operation includes an outbox record in the same database transaction.
steps: Save revision-2 and commit.
Open a new connection and read the draft, revision history and outbox.
expectedOutcome: revision-2 and exactly one corresponding outbox intent are committed together; revision-1 remains in history.
evidence: Transaction trace, persisted revision identities and matching outbox rows.

cases.title: Resume an interrupted migration without reseeding duplicates

scope.reference: G-02 PostgreSQL/EF Core persistence, non-security soft-delete filtering, direct SQL, transactions, concurrency and migrations. Tenant filtering depends on AC-004.

preconditions: A module migration adds a nullable field and an idempotent system seed to a populated PostgreSQL database; its recovery plan is recorded.
steps: Interrupt after a migration checkpoint and before completion is recorded.
Restart the coordinator, reconcile database and progress state, and run the migration and seed again.
expectedOutcome: The coordinator reports the interrupted operation and follows the supported resume or forward-repair path.
Existing rows survive, the new field has the planned shape, the seed exists once and migration progress reaches complete.
evidence: Checkpoint and migration history, repair/resume report, schema comparison and seed counts.

cases.title: Recover a website schema migration interruption

scope.website: W PostgreSQL transactions and optimistic concurrency for content and contact state, with migration recovery on the single database.

preconditions: A supported migration extends the article schema while old revisions and the active publication manifest remain present; a coordinated backup exists.
steps: Stop the migration process at its declared checkpoint.
Restart and reconcile progress, applying its supported resume or restore plan.
Read old and new revision fixtures and the active manifest.
expectedOutcome: Recovery reaches a coherent schema version without losing historical revisions or the active manifest.
Progress and any repair action are explicit; an untested reverse migration is never treated as recovery.
evidence: Migration and backup identities, interruption checkpoint, recovered schema/revision hashes and manifest reference checks.

cases.title: Handle duplicate, late and reordered events explicitly

scope.reference: G-02 durable events on actual PostgreSQL, including outbox/inbox crashes, duplicate retention, ordering, retries and poison disposition.

preconditions: The consumer declares a 24-hour inbox retention window and monotonic projection versions; event-4 has version 4 and event-5 version 5.
steps: Deliver event-5 before event-4, then duplicate event-5 immediately and at 23:59:59 after its receipt.
Deliver it again at 24:00:01 after retention expiry and inspect the declared reconciliation behavior.
expectedOutcome: The late version cannot regress the projection and retained duplicate receipts produce no additional effect.

After receipt expiry, reconciliation uses the stored projection version 5: replay leaves its value and effect count unchanged. The report distinguishes that version guard from the expired inbox guarantee.
evidence: Envelope order/times, retained and expired receipt observations, projection versions and reconciliation result.

cases.title: Deduplicate contact intent and ignore old publication generations

scope.website: W publication and contact outbox/inbox delivery, with duplicate and reordered effects on one site; no search propagation or arbitrary exactly-once email claim.

preconditions: The active site progresses from manifest-1 to manifest-2; both publication events and a contact-1 event are within the declared inbox retention period.
steps: Deliver manifest-2's event before manifest-1's, then deliver each twice.
Deliver contact-1's event three times.
expectedOutcome: The delivery cache converges to manifest-2 without reverting to manifest-1.
contact-1 produces one durable email intent; downstream delivery status remains separate.
evidence: Ordered event transcript, cache generation observations and contact intent/receipt counts.

cases.title: Keep an unsupported event from changing its projection

scope.reference: G-02 durable events on actual PostgreSQL, including outbox/inbox crashes, duplicate retention, ordering, retries and poison disposition.

preconditions: The consumer supports event schema 1; event-2 uses schema 2 and a later event-3 uses supported schema 1.
steps: Deliver event-2 through the normal transport and let the declared retry policy finish.
Deliver event-3 and inspect both dispositions.
expectedOutcome: event-2 has a visible unsupported-version failure and poison disposition without projection mutation.
event-3 completes; the failed event remains inspectable rather than disappearing.
evidence: Version contract, retry history, poison record and projection comparison.

cases.title: Surface poison publication and contact events

scope.website: W publication and contact outbox/inbox delivery, with duplicate and reordered effects on one site; no search propagation or arbitrary exactly-once email claim.

preconditions: The cache and contact consumers each have an event with an unsupported schema version; valid events for other records remain queued.
steps: Drain deliveries through the declared retry limit.
Inspect failed-event records and process the valid events.
expectedOutcome: Invalid events reach visible failed or poison states without changing cache or creating email intent.
Unrelated valid events finish, and the failed committed intents remain available for explicit repair.
evidence: Per-event retry/disposition history and cache/email-intent counts.

cases.title: Deliver one committed integration intent

scope.reference: G-02 durable events on actual PostgreSQL, including outbox/inbox crashes, duplicate retention, ordering, retries and poison disposition.

preconditions: Updating item-1 emits event-1; a consumer writes projection-1 and an inbox receipt atomically.
steps: Commit the update and allow dispatch and consumption.
Compare the business transaction, outbox envelope and inbox receipt.
expectedOutcome: The immutable event identity and supported schema version survive dispatch.
One projection effect and one completed receipt correspond to the committed intent.
evidence: Transaction/outbox linkage, transported envelope and projection/receipt records.

cases.title: Dispatch publication and contact intents

scope.website: W publication and contact outbox/inbox delivery, with duplicate and reordered effects on one site; no search propagation or arbitrary exactly-once email claim.

preconditions: manifest-2 activation and contact-1 acceptance each produce a durable event; cache and email-intent consumers use recorded inbox identities.
steps: Activate manifest-2 and accept contact-1 in separate transactions.
Dispatch both events and inspect the cache version and queued email intent.
expectedOutcome: The cache references manifest-2 and contact-1 has one delivery intent.
Each effect traces back to its committed producer state and immutable event identity.
evidence: Manifest/contact commit records, event envelopes and consumer receipts.

cases.title: Reconcile every durable-delivery crash window

scope.reference: G-02 durable events on actual PostgreSQL, including outbox/inbox crashes, duplicate retention, ordering, retries and poison disposition.

preconditions: Use a fresh item, event and consumer projection for each run; PostgreSQL owns both business/outbox and consumer/inbox transactions.
steps: Crash before producer commit; after producer commit before dispatch; after transport receipt before dispatch acknowledgement; during consumer work before commit; and after consumer commit before acknowledgement.
Restart dispatch and consumption after each fault and drain the queue.
expectedOutcome: The precommit run has no committed intent or effect.
Every committed intent eventually has a completed disposition; repeated delivery after either acknowledgement loss cannot duplicate the committed projection effect.
evidence: Five fault-point traces, business/outbox/inbox row sets, delivery attempts and final effect counts.

cases.title: Recover website dispatch and consumer acknowledgement loss

scope.website: W publication and contact outbox/inbox delivery, with duplicate and reordered effects on one site; no search propagation or arbitrary exactly-once email claim.

preconditions: Separate publication and contact fixtures have known committed state; the delivery adapter's reconciliation policy is recorded.
steps: For each fixture interrupt before producer commit, after commit before dispatch, after transport receipt before acknowledgement, before consumer commit and after consumer commit before acknowledgement.
Restart and reconcile the original event identities before retrying.
expectedOutcome: Precommit runs leave no intent; committed runs retain all intents until resolved.
Cache converges to the active manifest and contact intent is not duplicated; ambiguous external email delivery stays pending reconciliation.
evidence: Ten fault-point results, outbox/inbox identities, final cache/contact state and any transport reconciliation record.

cases.title: Resolve daylight-saving and misfire edges

scope.reference: Reference single-host scheduler qualification alongside the G-02 events/jobs contract: time, retries, cancellation, ownership and restart; no distributed topology claim.

preconditions: A test schedule uses America/Chicago; the advertised fixture policy skips nonexistent times, uses the first ambiguous occurrence and runs one catch-up after a misfire.
steps: Stop the worker across three due occurrences, then restart after the third.
expectedOutcome: The nonexistent occurrence is visibly skipped; the ambiguous occurrence resolves once to 2026-11-01T06:30:00Z.
Misfire history lists the missed occurrences and one catch-up execution, matching the recorded policy.
evidence: Local/UTC resolution table, supported policy configuration and misfire/attempt history.

cases.title: Keep publication deterministic across local-time changes

scope.website: W scheduled publication on the single host, including retries, cancellation, timezone transitions, misfires, lease loss and restart.

preconditions: The publication scheduler advertises the fixture policy: skip nonexistent local times, choose the first ambiguous occurrence and perform one catch-up for missed occurrences in America/Chicago.
steps: Resolve schedules at 2026-03-08 02:30 and 2026-11-01 01:30.
Restart the scheduler after missing three scheduled instants for one release.
expectedOutcome: The first local time is skipped with a reason; the second resolves once to 06:30Z.
The missed release activates at most once through the one-catch-up policy; each skipped occurrence has a visible outcome.
evidence: Timezone policy, UTC resolutions, misfire decisions and publication activation count.

cases.title: Report exhausted retries and both cancellation modes

scope.reference: Reference single-host scheduler qualification alongside the G-02 events/jobs contract: time, retries, cancellation, ownership and restart; no distributed topology claim.

preconditions: job-2 fails deterministically with a declared three-attempt retry limit; job-3 is queued and job-4 is paused while running before its effect.
steps: Run job-2 through all three attempts.
Cancel job-3 before dispatch; request cancellation of running job-4 and release its pause.
expectedOutcome: job-2 ends failed after exactly three attempts with its cause recorded.
job-3 never starts; job-4 reports cooperative cancellation separately from prevention of dispatch and records whether any effect committed.
evidence: Retry configuration, attempt timestamps, cancellation acknowledgements and final effect counts.

cases.title: Expose publication retry failure and cancellation

scope.website: W scheduled publication on the single host, including retries, cancellation, timezone transitions, misfires, lease loss and restart.

preconditions: Three separate publication jobs are available: one with a dependency failure and a three-attempt limit, one queued, and one running before activation commit.
steps: Exhaust the failed job's retries.
Cancel the queued job and request cooperative cancellation of the running job before releasing its commit pause.
expectedOutcome: The failure preserves the prior active manifest and records three failed attempts.
Queued cancellation prevents execution; running cancellation reports its final disposition, with no unreported activation.
evidence: Per-job retry/cancellation records and active-manifest histories.

cases.title: Execute a due job once with visible state

scope.reference: Reference single-host scheduler qualification alongside the G-02 events/jobs contract: time, retries, cancellation, ownership and restart; no distributed topology claim.

preconditions: job-1 is persisted for 2026-11-01T12:00:00Z with an idempotent counter effect and no existing attempt.
steps: Advance the controlled clock to one second before the due time, then to the due instant.
Let the worker complete and inspect job history.
expectedOutcome: No execution occurs early.
One queued-to-running-to-completed sequence and one counter effect appear at or after the due instant.
evidence: Persisted schedule, clock trace, attempt history and counter value.

cases.title: Activate an exact scheduled publication

scope.website: W scheduled publication on the single host, including retries, cancellation, timezone transitions, misfires, lease loss and restart.

preconditions: manifest-2 is validated and scheduled for 2026-11-01T12:00:00Z; manifest-1 is currently active.
steps: Read the site just before the scheduled instant.
Advance to the due instant, run the scheduler and read again.
expectedOutcome: manifest-1 serves the earlier read and manifest-2 serves the later read.
One completed job binds exactly manifest-2, without resolving a newer draft.
evidence: Schedule identity, job history, active-pointer transitions and response manifest identities.

cases.title: Recover a job after lease loss and restart

scope.reference: Reference single-host scheduler qualification alongside the G-02 events/jobs contract: time, retries, cancellation, ownership and restart; no distributed topology claim.

preconditions: job-5 pauses before committing its counter effect; one worker owns a lease and a replacement worker can run on the same host.
steps: Expire the first lease, restart ownership processing and let the replacement acquire it.
Release the stale worker, then complete the replacement attempt.
expectedOutcome: Only the valid attempt can commit the counter effect; stale ownership cannot commit a competing result.
History identifies lease loss and the replacement attempt; the job ends completed with one effect.
evidence: Lease identities/times, commit concurrency results and final job/counter records.

cases.title: Reconcile lease loss at publication commit

scope.website: W scheduled publication on the single host, including retries, cancellation, timezone transitions, misfires, lease loss and restart.

preconditions: A scheduled job for manifest-2 pauses just before activation; manifest-1 is active and the lease has a controlled expiry.
steps: Expire the lease and start a replacement worker on the same host.
Release both workers, then restart once after activation commits but before job completion acknowledgement.
expectedOutcome: The active pointer reaches manifest-2 once through a valid concurrency-checked transition.
Retry recognizes the committed activation; history records stale ownership and reconciliation without duplicate publication.
evidence: Lease and activation identities, commit results, restart trace and completed job history.

cases.title: Respect compatibility and cancellation boundaries

scope.reference: G-02 advertised .NET and TypeScript client modes, public version/error contracts and cancellation. Authentication and access decisions are supplied by AC-002 and AC-003.

preconditions: The release declares its oldest supported API contract and current contract. A controlled update can pause before commit or after commit before response.
steps: Read through the oldest supported and current versions, then the immediately unsupported predecessor.
Cancel one update before commit and cancel another after commit but before its response; query each operation's authoritative status.
expectedOutcome: Supported versions preserve their declared fields; the unsupported version reports a compatibility failure.
Precommit cancellation leaves no change; postcommit cancellation does not claim rollback and reports the committed outcome through reconciliation.
evidence: Compatibility declaration, version transcripts, cancellation timing and authoritative operation-state reads.

cases.title: Check W client version and cancellation edges

scope.website: Only W minimal Admin and Razor delivery API contracts: typed errors, compatibility and cancellation; no GraphQL or broader client-surface claim.

preconditions: The W release advertises current and oldest-supported endpoint versions; a draft save can pause either side of its database commit.
steps: Read through both supported versions and the first unsupported predecessor.
Cancel one save before commit and another after commit before response, then inspect operation status.
expectedOutcome: Supported clients retain the declared revision fields and unsupported versions fail explicitly.
Cancellation before commit preserves the old draft; cancellation after commit is reconciled as committed rather than silently retried as a new save.
evidence: Version matrix, cancellation traces and draft/operation state for both fault points.

cases.title: Return actionable typed contract failures

scope.reference: G-02 advertised .NET and TypeScript client modes, public version/error contracts and cancellation. Authentication and access decisions are supplied by AC-002 and AC-003.

preconditions: A title field is required; a known stale token and an unsupported API version are prepared. Dynamic discovery is exercised only if advertised.
steps: Submit a missing title, then a stale write, then an unsupported API version from every advertised client.
For dynamic clients, separately make discovery unavailable and supply an unresolvable endpoint binding.
expectedOutcome: Validation, concurrency and version failures retain distinct stable codes and correlation identifiers without a successful write.
Advertised dynamic clients distinguish discovery failure from endpoint-resolution failure.
evidence: Input/error matrix, typed client exceptions or results, and unchanged record versions.

cases.title: Show distinct validation, conflict and version errors

scope.website: Only W minimal Admin and Razor delivery API contracts: typed errors, compatibility and cancellation; no GraphQL or broader client-surface claim.

preconditions: A contact field is required; article-1 has a stale saved token available; the W client's supported API version is known.
steps: Submit contact without its required message.
Save article-1 with the stale token.
Call a W endpoint using an unsupported version.
expectedOutcome: Each operation produces its declared typed error and correlation identifier; Admin presents the field or conflict context.
None of the failures creates a contact, revision or publication.
evidence: Three endpoint responses, UI error observations and authoritative row counts.

cases.title: Complete the same operation through advertised clients

scope.reference: G-02 advertised .NET and TypeScript client modes, public version/error contracts and cancellation. Authentication and access decisions are supplied by AC-002 and AC-003.

preconditions: The release enumerates its advertised generated, static and dynamic .NET/TypeScript client modes against a pinned endpoint contract. item-1 has a title, optional note and version token.
steps: For every advertised mode, read item-1, update its title with the current token and read it again.
Compare the endpoint inventory and serialized values across modes.
expectedOutcome: Every advertised client preserves typed fields, optional-value meaning and the returned version.
The inventory and client contract agree on route, method and version for each exercised operation.
evidence: Client-mode matrix, contract digest and request/response transcripts with typed assertions.

cases.title: Carry website revision contracts through Admin and delivery

scope.website: Only W minimal Admin and Razor delivery API contracts: typed errors, compatibility and cancellation; no GraphQL or broader client-surface claim.

preconditions: W's endpoint inventory names the Admin draft-save and Razor publication-read operations. The TypeScript client and server-side delivery adapter use the same pinned contracts.
steps: Save article-1 as revision-2 through Admin and inspect its typed response.
Read the separately published revision-1 through the delivery contract.
expectedOutcome: Admin receives revision-2's identity and concurrency token; delivery receives the active manifest's revision-1.
Serialization preserves stable content and revision identities across the two contracts.
evidence: W endpoint inventory, contract digest, client traces and revision-id assertions.

cases.title: Recover a client after an interrupted response

scope.reference: G-02 advertised .NET and TypeScript client modes, public version/error contracts and cancellation. Authentication and access decisions are supplied by AC-002 and AC-003.

preconditions: An idempotent create operation uses operation-1 and has committed item-2; the response is interrupted. Each advertised client mode gets an independent fixture.
steps: Reconnect, inspect operation-1 and retry using the same operation identity under the endpoint's declared contract.
Read the created item and compare versions.
expectedOutcome: The client recovers the committed result without creating a second item.
A new correlation for the retry retains linkage to operation-1 and its single final disposition.
evidence: Interrupted request, reconciliation/retry transcript and item/operation counts.

cases.title: Recover the Admin after losing a save response

scope.website: Only W minimal Admin and Razor delivery API contracts: typed errors, compatibility and cancellation; no GraphQL or broader client-surface claim.

preconditions: Admin has article-1 open and save operation-2 is accepted; its response is interrupted after commit.
steps: Reconnect and resolve operation-2, then reload the returned revision.
Retry only under the same operation identity if the endpoint requires retry.
expectedOutcome: The UI displays the committed revision and clears its uncertain-save state.
The history contains one revision for operation-2 and no duplicate save effect.
evidence: Browser state transitions, operation lookup/retry transcript and revision history.

cases.title: Enforce declared file size and cancellation boundaries

scope.reference: G-02 filesystem Files byte/metadata integrity, immutable versions, size/cancellation boundaries, interrupted writes and restore. Eligibility and access outcomes are prerequisites from the security families.

preconditions: The upload fixture configures a supported 1,024-byte maximum. Inputs contain 1,023, 1,024 and 1,025 bytes; a fourth upload can pause before finalization.
steps: Complete each size variant and compare metadata.
Cancel the fourth upload before finalization and inspect temporary and authoritative storage.
expectedOutcome: The first two sizes complete; 1,025 bytes reports the declared size limit without a completed version.
The canceled upload has a visible canceled disposition and no authoritative partial version.
evidence: Configured limit, per-size outcomes, cancellation trace and storage/version inventories.

cases.title: Check the content-package media size edge

scope.website: W upload/import through filesystem Files, versioned editorial metadata, package-byte integrity, interrupted storage and restore. Scanning/quarantine, denied access and revocation are supplied by AC-003 and AC-031.

preconditions: Three otherwise valid eligible image fixtures have exact sizes of 10 MiB minus one byte, 10 MiB and 10 MiB plus one byte; manifest sizes and hashes match. Deployment capacity supports the contract limit.
steps: Dry-run each package and apply only the two supported-size plans through Files.
expectedOutcome: The first two sizes pass the format size check and retain exact stored lengths.
The final size is rejected as over the package media limit before apply.
evidence: Byte counts and digests, dry-run diagnostics and stored version sizes.

cases.title: Reject an integrity mismatch without replacing stored bytes

scope.reference: G-02 filesystem Files byte/metadata integrity, immutable versions, size/cancellation boundaries, interrupted writes and restore. Eligibility and access outcomes are prerequisites from the security families.

preconditions: asset-1 has a complete version; a new upload declares the digest of fixture A while carrying different fixture B bytes.
steps: Attempt to complete the mismatched upload.
Inspect the operation diagnostic, authoritative version list and existing version bytes.
expectedOutcome: Completion reports the digest mismatch and does not add a completed version.
The prior version remains readable with its original digest; staged-byte disposition is explicit.
evidence: Expected/observed digest comparison, completion result and version/storage inventory.

cases.title: Reject damaged package media before completion

scope.website: W upload/import through filesystem Files, versioned editorial metadata, package-byte integrity, interrupted storage and restore. Scanning/quarantine, denied access and revocation are supplied by AC-003 and AC-031.

preconditions: A valid package declares the minimal image's byte length and SHA-256; one copy has a changed byte and another a truncated file.
steps: Validate and attempt import of each copy.
Inspect content mappings, Files versions and the prior active publication.
expectedOutcome: Each copy reports its exact integrity discrepancy before authoritative apply.
No new completed media version, content mapping or publication is created.
evidence: Two integrity diagnostics and unchanged mapping/version/manifest inventories.

cases.title: Preserve logical file identity across immutable versions

scope.reference: G-02 filesystem Files byte/metadata integrity, immutable versions, size/cancellation boundaries, interrupted writes and restore. Eligibility and access outcomes are prerequisites from the security families.

preconditions: A filesystem-backed logical asset asset-1 accepts a 512-byte fixture and a distinct 768-byte fixture; eligibility decisions are already supplied by AC-031.
steps: Upload the first fixture, then create a second version under asset-1.
Stream each exact version and inspect metadata.
expectedOutcome: Both versions retain their own byte lengths and SHA-256 digests; reading the old version still returns the old bytes.
asset-1 remains the same logical identity while physical versions differ.
evidence: Source/read-back digests, metadata records and version identity history.

cases.title: Keep imported and uploaded media versions reproducible

scope.website: W upload/import through filesystem Files, versioned editorial metadata, package-byte integrity, interrupted storage and restore. Scanning/quarantine, denied access and revocation are supplied by AC-003 and AC-031.

preconditions: The minimal content-package image and its exact hash/size form one fixture. A second eligible image version and descriptive alt text are prepared under the same logical asset.
steps: Import the first version through Files, then upload the second.
Read each version by its identity and inspect its dimensions, media type, alt text and byte digest.
expectedOutcome: Both versions preserve their own bytes and metadata; changing the current version does not rewrite the historical one.
Editorial placement resolves the selected asset version.
evidence: Package and Files metadata, source/read-back digests and editorial reference identities.

cases.title: Reconcile interrupted filesystem writes and restore versions

scope.reference: G-02 filesystem Files byte/metadata integrity, immutable versions, size/cancellation boundaries, interrupted writes and restore. Eligibility and access outcomes are prerequisites from the security families.

preconditions: asset-1 has two complete versions with captured digests in a coordinated backup. A third upload can stop midstream or after bytes are staged but before metadata commit.
steps: Interrupt at each point in independent runs, restart storage handling and reconcile the operation identity.
Restore the backed-up metadata and bytes into the recovery fixture and read both historical versions.
expectedOutcome: No partial upload becomes a completed version; retry or cleanup accounts for staged bytes without deleting referenced versions.
Restored versions match the backup's identities, lengths and digests.
evidence: Fault-point traces, staged-object reconciliation report, backup identity and restored read-back digests.

cases.title: Recover imported media after a filesystem interruption

scope.website: W upload/import through filesystem Files, versioned editorial metadata, package-byte integrity, interrupted storage and restore. Scanning/quarantine, denied access and revocation are supplied by AC-003 and AC-031.

preconditions: A reviewed import stages new media while a prior publication retains old versions; the database/Files backup identifies all historical references.
steps: Stop storage midwrite, then separately after staging before database commit.
Reconcile each import by its original operation identity, complete or clean its unreferenced staging, and restore the coordinated backup into the recovery fixture.
expectedOutcome: Each interrupted import reaches a reported final disposition without a dangling completed media reference.
The restored active and historical manifests resolve to the original version hashes.
evidence: Import recovery reports, staged/committed inventories and restored manifest-to-media integrity results.

cases.title: Keep duplicate and ambiguous transport outcomes distinct

scope.website: W contact email only through the release-selected transport: durable intent, acceptance/queue/delivery/failure states, duplicates and outage recovery. Destination authority is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: contact-3 uses one recorded delivery identity; the transport can acknowledge acceptance without confirming delivery.
steps: Deliver the same contact event three times.
Return transport acceptance without a delivery confirmation, then repeat its acceptance notification.
expectedOutcome: One message intent and one reconciled dispatch identity remain.
Repeated acceptance notifications do not add messages or promote the delivery state to confirmed.
evidence: Duplicate-event/notification transcript, intent/dispatch counts and final delivery state.

cases.title: Retain a failed contact delivery without a false success

scope.website: W contact email only through the release-selected transport: durable intent, acceptance/queue/delivery/failure states, duplicates and outage recovery. Destination authority is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: The selected transport fixture returns a permanent address-delivery failure for contact-2; destination authority has already been qualified separately.
steps: Dispatch contact-2 and inspect its terminal disposition through the minimal Admin.
expectedOutcome: The durable request remains accepted while email delivery is failed with an actionable reason.
The interface does not label either queueing or transport rejection as delivered.
evidence: Transport failure result, durable request and delivery-state history, and Admin observation.

cases.title: Track contact intent through provider confirmation

scope.website: W contact email only through the release-selected transport: durable intent, acceptance/queue/delivery/failure states, duplicates and outage recovery. Destination authority is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: contact-1 has a prequalified configured destination and an eligible durable email intent. The bounded transport fixture declares whether confirmed delivery is observable.
steps: Accept contact-1, queue and dispatch its message.
Observe transport acceptance and, only where supported, the later delivery confirmation.
expectedOutcome: Durable request acceptance, queued dispatch and transport acceptance have distinct recorded states.
Delivered appears only with the transport's positive confirmation; otherwise delivery remains unconfirmed.
evidence: Request/intent identity chain, timestamps, transport acknowledgement and any confirmation record.

cases.title: Reconcile contact delivery after an outage

scope.website: W contact email only through the release-selected transport: durable intent, acceptance/queue/delivery/failure states, duplicates and outage recovery. Destination authority is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: contact-4 is queued; use separate fixtures for transport unavailable before send and connection lost after provider acceptance before local acknowledgement.
steps: Trigger each fault and restart dispatch.
Resolve the original transport identity using its advertised reconciliation capability before any resend; resume when the outcome is known.
expectedOutcome: The unsent fixture eventually dispatches under the original intent.
The ambiguous fixture stays visibly unresolved until reconciled; no blind retry creates an additional message, and resolved acceptance is retained.
evidence: Outage/timeout traces, retry schedule, reconciliation response and final message counts.

cases.title: Keep schema and preview versions pinned at an edit boundary

scope.website: W versioned content types, fields and references, typed composition, revision conflicts and exact-revision preview. Preview authorization is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: article-1 revision-1 uses schema version 1. A compatible schema version 2 adds an optional summary field while both renderers remain installed.
steps: Save revision-2 against schema version 2 with the summary absent.
Open preview explicitly for revision-1, save revision-3, and refresh that preview.
Propose a narrowing schema change against existing values.
expectedOutcome: Absence of the optional summary is preserved and historical revision-1 retains schema version 1.
The selected preview still renders revision-1; narrowing reports affected content for a migration decision rather than discarding values.
evidence: Schema versions, stored field snapshots, preview revision identities and incompatibility report.

cases.title: Reject invalid fields, references and stale authoring

scope.website: W versioned content types, fields and references, typed composition, revision conflicts and exact-revision preview. Preview authorization is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: article-1 has a current version; two authors opened the preceding version. The valid type and renderer fixtures are retained.
steps: Independently submit a missing required title, an integer title, a missing content reference and an unavailable block version.
Save from author A, then submit author B's stale token.
expectedOutcome: Each invalid draft reports its field/reference/dependency diagnostic.
The stale write produces a visible conflict; none of the rejected inputs silently replaces the current valid revision.
evidence: Invalid-input matrix, diagnostics, conflict display and retained revision hashes.

cases.title: Save and preview a precisely selected composed revision

scope.website: W versioned content types, fields and references, typed composition, revision conflicts and exact-revision preview. Preview authorization is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: The article type version 1 has required title and a content reference to page-1. Installed version-1 block, layout and template renderers support a heading and paragraph.
steps: Create article-1 using the reference and two ordered typed blocks; save revision-1.
Change its paragraph and save revision-2.
Preview revision-1 and compare both revisions.
expectedOutcome: Each revision retains its schema and renderer dependencies, field values and block order.
Preview shows revision-1 exactly and comparison identifies the paragraph change without changing production publication.
evidence: Typed revisions and dependency identities, comparison output and preview-selected revision observations.

cases.title: Preserve typed taxonomy references during authoring

scope.website: W versioned content types, fields and references, typed composition, revision conflicts and exact-revision preview. Preview authorization is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: Taxonomy garden has parent term crops and child term herbs. The article type declares a term reference targeting garden; both terms have stable identities.
steps: Save article-1 revision-1 referencing herbs.
Change the display label of herbs, save article-1 as revision-2 and compare the typed references in both revisions.
expectedOutcome: The term reference resolves within garden and its parent relationship remains crops.
The label edit does not replace the term identity; both article revisions retain the same stable reference while their own revision identities remain distinct.
evidence: Taxonomy identities and parent graph, stored field references and article revision comparison.

cases.title: Recover an interrupted save and restore an older revision as a draft

scope.website: W versioned content types, fields and references, typed composition, revision conflicts and exact-revision preview. Preview authorization is supplied by AC-003.

preconditions: article-1 has revisions 1 and 2; an autosave operation-3 can lose its response after commit.
steps: Interrupt the response and reconnect using operation-3's status.
Restore revision-1 as a new draft, validate it against its supported schema and compare history.
expectedOutcome: Reconciliation identifies exactly one saved revision for operation-3.
Restore creates a distinct validated draft; it does not overwrite revisions 1 or 2 or activate a publication.
evidence: Autosave/reconnect history, operation identity, revision comparison and publication pointer before/after.

cases.title: Resolve competing activations at one schedule instant

scope.website: W immutable publication manifests, scheduled activation, withdrawal/rollback, unique routes and cache convergence on one site/culture; search propagation is excluded.

preconditions: Two validated releases target the same site/culture at 2026-11-01T12:00:00Z and expect the same active-manifest token.
steps: Read before the due instant, then let both jobs attempt activation at that instant.
Read repeatedly during activation and cache convergence.
expectedOutcome: No release activates early.
One concurrency-checked activation wins; the other has an explicit conflict. Requests never combine the two manifests, and cache convergence refers to the winning generation.
evidence: Schedule and expected-version inputs, competing commit outcomes and response/cache generation timeline.

cases.title: Reject competing route owners without replacing publication

scope.website: W immutable publication manifests, scheduled activation, withdrawal/rollback, unique routes and cache convergence on one site/culture; search propagation is excluded.

preconditions: manifest-1 is active. A proposed release gives two different entries the canonical route /guide; another depends on an absent retained asset version.
steps: Validate and attempt activation of each proposed release.
expectedOutcome: Route collision and missing dependency produce distinct diagnostics naming the conflicting references.
Neither failed release replaces manifest-1 or changes its route table.
evidence: Invalid manifests, validation reports and unchanged active pointer/routes.

cases.title: Publish a frozen manifest and later withdraw it

scope.website: W immutable publication manifests, scheduled activation, withdrawal/rollback, unique routes and cache convergence on one site/culture; search propagation is excluded.

preconditions: manifest-1 is active. manifest-2 binds article-1 revision-2, page-1 revision-1, exact asset versions and unique route/navigation metadata.
steps: Activate manifest-2 and read both routes, including a request spanning activation.
Draft article-1 revision-3, then withdraw the published release and inspect authoritative delivery and convergence status.
expectedOutcome: Each request resolves one consistent manifest and the later draft does not mutate manifest-2.
Withdrawal has an explicit recorded state and delivery follows it; immutable manifests and their revision history remain retained.
evidence: Manifest hashes, active-pointer/withdrawal history, per-request manifest identities and propagation status.

cases.title: Roll back after failed activation and interrupted propagation

scope.website: W immutable publication manifests, scheduled activation, withdrawal/rollback, unique routes and cache convergence on one site/culture; search propagation is excluded.

preconditions: manifest-1 and its compatible schemas/renderers/media are retained. manifest-2 is validated; cache propagation can pause after an authoritative switch.
steps: First inject a failure before the activation commit and inspect the pointer.
In a separate run activate manifest-2, interrupt cache propagation, restart the consumer, then explicitly roll back to validated manifest-1.
expectedOutcome: Precommit activation failure leaves manifest-1 active.
Restart and rollback converge caches to the selected authoritative manifest with visible pending/failed/completed status; no historical manifest is edited.
evidence: Fault traces, immutable manifest hashes, rollback transaction and cache convergence observations.

cases.title: Keep delivery and discovery on the selected publication

scope.website: W Razor delivery for one site/culture with prequalified aliases and media decisions, installed renderers and discovery derived from the active publication. Host manipulation and protected-content boundaries remain AC-004/AC-031 work.

preconditions: article-1 revision-1 is published at /guide; revision-2 changes title and slug but remains a draft. The protected preview fixture is supplied by AC-003.
steps: Read /guide, canonical metadata and sitemap while creating the draft.
Publish revision-2 with a declared route move and inspect delivery and discovery after convergence.
expectedOutcome: Before activation the three public outputs still describe revision-1's published route and title.
After convergence they consistently describe revision-2; a draft save alone does not update the public projection.
evidence: Published/draft revision ids, response/SEO/sitemap snapshots and publication-generation timeline.

cases.title: Refuse a release with an unavailable Razor renderer

scope.website: W Razor delivery for one site/culture with prequalified aliases and media decisions, installed renderers and discovery derived from the active publication. Host manipulation and protected-content boundaries remain AC-004/AC-031 work.

preconditions: manifest-1 renders with installed template version 1; proposed manifest-2 requires absent template version 2.
steps: Validate the proposal and attempt activation.
Request the currently published page after the failure.
expectedOutcome: Validation identifies the missing renderer and blocks activation.
Existing delivery still uses manifest-1 and its installed renderer, with no partial template substitution.
evidence: Renderer dependency diagnostic, active pointer and postfailure response.

cases.title: Render one publication through canonical and alias bindings

scope.website: W Razor delivery for one site/culture with prequalified aliases and media decisions, installed renderers and discovery derived from the active publication. Host manipulation and protected-content boundaries remain AC-004/AC-031 work.

preconditions: One site in en-US has a canonical binding and two already qualified alias bindings. manifest-1 selects page-1 and a versioned eligible image with alt text.
steps: Request page-1 through each binding using the configured Razor renderer.
Inspect response content, media version, canonical metadata and sitemap entry.
expectedOutcome: Every binding resolves the same site, culture and selected revision.
The page uses the declared media version and the configured canonical origin; metadata and sitemap reference the selected publication.
evidence: Binding inventory, rendered responses, media digest and canonical/sitemap observations.

cases.title: Rebuild Razor delivery cache from the active manifest

scope.website: W Razor delivery for one site/culture with prequalified aliases and media decisions, installed renderers and discovery derived from the active publication. Host manipulation and protected-content boundaries remain AC-004/AC-031 work.

preconditions: manifest-2 is active with retained schema, renderer and Files versions; derived delivery cache contains an older generation.
steps: Interrupt cache rebuild, discard only derived cache state and restart rendering.
Read each published route through canonical and qualified alias bindings.
expectedOutcome: Rebuild converges to manifest-2 from authoritative data without changing publication history.
All sampled pages and media references use one internally consistent active-manifest generation.
evidence: Rebuild checkpoints, authoritative hashes and route/media response comparisons.

cases.title: Apply declared navigation and redirect limits

scope.website: W blog, pinned Git documentation, taxonomy/navigation, SEO/redirects and contact journeys; one site/culture and no engagement, search or newsletters.

preconditions: Version-1 packages contain valid navigation trees of depth 16 and 17 and redirect chains of length 16 and 17, each ending at a real route.
steps: Dry-run each independent variant.
Publish the valid variants and follow their final navigation target and redirect chain; also inspect the configured query-discard behavior.
expectedOutcome: Depth/length 16 validates and resolves the declared target; 17 is rejected before apply.
Redirect resolution follows the configured same-site status/target rules and drops incoming query data as the package contract declares.
evidence: Exact trees/chains, boundary diagnostics and redirect/navigation request transcripts.

cases.title: Reject broken navigation, redirects and documentation sources

scope.website: W blog, pinned Git documentation, taxonomy/navigation, SEO/redirects and contact journeys; one site/culture and no engagement, search or newsletters.

preconditions: A valid W content graph and publication are available as the control fixture.
steps: Independently remove a referenced entry, make menu A parent B and B parent A, and create redirects /old to /older and /older to /old.
Separately name an unconfigured documentation repository binding.
expectedOutcome: Validation reports the missing reference, complete menu cycle, redirect loop and unresolved documentation source.
None of these proposals changes published navigation, routes or documentation.
evidence: Four invalid graph/source inputs, diagnostics and unchanged publication hashes.

cases.title: Read a blog post through taxonomy and ordered navigation

scope.website: W blog, pinned Git documentation, taxonomy/navigation, SEO/redirects and contact journeys; one site/culture and no engagement, search or newsletters.

preconditions: Two published posts, harvest-1 and harvest-2, share term garden. Navigation has Home then Journal, with Journal targeting the blog listing.
steps: Open Journal, select garden and read each post.
Reorder the two navigation entries through Admin, publish the navigation change and repeat the journey.
expectedOutcome: The listing links to both published posts and the selected term is preserved.
Published navigation follows the new sibling order and all links resolve to their intended entries.
evidence: Term and navigation identities, ordered published navigation and browser journey observations.

cases.title: Read two documentation versions and submit contact

scope.website: W blog, pinned Git documentation, taxonomy/navigation, SEO/redirects and contact journeys; one site/culture and no engagement, search or newsletters.

preconditions: Two documentation versions use distinct entry keys/routes and pinned commits from a locally available configured repository binding. A contact page uses a prequalified named destination.
steps: Import the already captured documentation snapshots, publish them and read both versions.
Follow the contact route, submit a valid request and inspect its durable receipt and delivery status.
expectedOutcome: Each documentation route resolves its own version and pinned-source identity.
Contact creates one durable request; the visitor receipt does not claim confirmed email delivery.
evidence: Source-version/commit mapping, rendered version pages and contact receipt/state linkage.

cases.title: Recover an interrupted documentation and navigation import

scope.website: W blog, pinned Git documentation, taxonomy/navigation, SEO/redirects and contact journeys; one site/culture and no engagement, search or newsletters.

preconditions: Version v1 documentation and ordered navigation are published. A reviewed package introduces v2 with distinct entry keys and revised navigation; its snapshots are already local.
steps: Interrupt apply before database commit, then reconcile and resume using the original operation identity.
Validate and publish the completed result, retaining v1.
expectedOutcome: The interruption preserves the prior published graph.
Recovery introduces v2 and its navigation once, retains v1 identities/routes and reports every mapped item's outcome.
evidence: Import checkpoints/result, stable-key mappings and browser reads of both documentation versions.

cases.title: Check field length and duplicate submission identity

scope.website: W contact fields, durable acceptance and duplicate suppression only; antispam, rate limits and recipient authorization are prerequisites from AC-003 and AC-031, not cases here.

preconditions: The fixture declares a supported 2,000-character message limit. Two tabs share the same submission identity and valid field values.
steps: Submit messages of 1,999, 2,000 and 2,001 characters using separate identities.
Submit the same valid request concurrently from both tabs, then reuse that identity with changed content.
expectedOutcome: The first two lengths pass field validation and the third fails without truncation.
Identical repeated intent resolves to one request/receipt; changed content under that identity yields an explicit conflict without replacing it.
evidence: Length/input matrix, concurrent responses and request/body digest counts.

cases.title: Reject contact field errors and absent routing configuration

scope.website: W contact fields, durable acceptance and duplicate suppression only; antispam, rate limits and recipient authorization are prerequisites from AC-003 and AC-031, not cases here.

preconditions: The form contract requires a nonempty message and a syntactically valid reply address. A separate fixture has no configured named destination.
steps: Submit a missing message, then an invalid reply-address syntax.
Submit valid fields against the fixture without a destination.
expectedOutcome: Field errors identify their fields and preserve entered values for correction.
Missing configuration returns an actionable unavailable outcome; none of the three attempts reports accepted or creates a dispatchable intent.
evidence: Validation/configuration diagnostics, rendered error states and durable request/intent counts.

cases.title: Accept one validated contact request durably

scope.website: W contact fields, durable acceptance and duplicate suppression only; antispam, rate limits and recipient authorization are prerequisites from AC-003 and AC-031, not cases here.

preconditions: The contact fixture has required message and reply-address fields, a prequalified named destination and passed security prerequisites. The email worker is paused.
steps: Submit a valid message through the public form.
Inspect the returned receipt, durable request and queued intent before releasing the worker.
expectedOutcome: Success is returned only for a durable request with one delivery intent.
The receipt says accepted without implying that email has already been delivered.
evidence: Field values with synthetic data, receipt identity and matching request/intent rows.

cases.title: Recover a contact submission with a lost acknowledgement

scope.website: W contact fields, durable acceptance and duplicate suppression only; antispam, rate limits and recipient authorization are prerequisites from AC-003 and AC-031, not cases here.

preconditions: contact-5 commits its request and outbox intent, but the HTTP response can be dropped; dispatch is paused.
steps: Drop the response after commit, restart the application and retry with the original submission identity.
Resume dispatch and inspect the durable receipt and downstream delivery state.
expectedOutcome: Retry recovers the same accepted request with no second intent.
Email proceeds independently through its observable states under AC-013, and acceptance is retained through restart.
evidence: Fault timing, retry/receipt transcript and before/after request, outbox and delivery identities.

cases.title: Inspect theme reflow, contrast and keyboard alternatives

scope.website: W minimal React/TypeScript Admin action ledger and original Razor theme, with keyboard, focus, assistive technology, contrast, responsive/error states and WCAG 2.2 AA evidence. Account and authority actions are supplied by security families.

preconditions: The declared W pages and Admin dialogs include the longest valid titles, populated validation messages and nested navigation. The test covers each advertised viewport/browser pairing.
steps: Inspect at 320 CSS pixels wide, 200 percent text size and 400 percent zoom using the applicable WCAG conditions.
Measure normal text, large text, controls and focus contrast; inspect target sizes and applicable exceptions.
Reorder blocks and navigation without dragging, traverse dialogs and return focus to their triggers.
expectedOutcome: Content and actions remain usable without unintended loss or two-dimensional scrolling where reflow applies.
Text and controls meet applicable 4.5:1 or 3:1 contrast criteria; focus/target-size findings are assessed against WCAG 2.2 AA.
Keyboard alternatives preserve order and dialog focus returns predictably.
evidence: Viewport/zoom captures, contrast measurements, criterion/exception decisions and keyboard ordering/focus results.

cases.title: Present validation and conflict failures accessibly

scope.website: W minimal React/TypeScript Admin action ledger and original Razor theme, with keyboard, focus, assistive technology, contrast, responsive/error states and WCAG 2.2 AA evidence. Account and authority actions are supplied by security families.

preconditions: The authoring form has a required title; a contact message is required; a stale draft token and conflicting route are available.
steps: Use only the keyboard to submit each invalid author/contact form, stale save and route collision.
Inspect error summaries, field associations, status announcements and focus, then correct each input.
expectedOutcome: Each failed operation is explained in text and programmatically associated with the affected input or action.
Entered data is retained, focus reaches the relevant error without a trap, and corrected submissions can complete.
evidence: Four error-state workflows, field/summary associations, focus sequence and assistive-technology observations.

cases.title: Complete the minimal action ledger and public journeys accessibly

scope.website: W minimal React/TypeScript Admin action ledger and original Razor theme, with keyboard, focus, assistive technology, contrast, responsive/error states and WCAG 2.2 AA evidence. Account and authority actions are supplied by security families.

preconditions: The W action ledger lists authoring, validation/conflicts, preview, schedule/publish/rollback, media, taxonomy/navigation, routes, contact delivery, import review and recovery. The original theme and each advertised browser/assistive-technology pairing are identified.
steps: Using keyboard and screen reader, author and compare a revision, inspect validation, resolve a prepared conflict and open its exact preview.
Schedule, publish and roll back a release; upload/select versioned media and edit taxonomy/navigation and routes.
Inspect contact delivery, review and apply an import plan, and inspect a recovery operation through their declared Admin routes.
On the public site, navigate home, blog listing/post, documentation versions and the contact form; submit a valid contact request.
expectedOutcome: Every listed action has a reachable declared route, usable accessible name/role/state and visible focus, with the expected domain outcome.
The ledger reports each action and browser/assistive-technology pairing separately; no missing action is counted as native completion.
evidence: Action-by-action ledger with route, inputs and outcomes.
Keyboard/focus traces, screen-reader observations and a criterion-level WCAG 2.2 AA assessment including manual findings.

cases.title: Recover an interrupted editor without losing work or focus

scope.website: W minimal React/TypeScript Admin action ledger and original Razor theme, with keyboard, focus, assistive technology, contrast, responsive/error states and WCAG 2.2 AA evidence. Account and authority actions are supplied by security families.

preconditions: An author has an unsaved paragraph and focused Save control; one save fixture fails before commit and another commits but loses its response.
steps: Interrupt each save and reconnect.
Resolve the recorded operation outcome, restore retained unsaved input where needed and complete the save.
Close any recovery dialog and continue editing by keyboard.
expectedOutcome: The UI distinguishes unsaved changes from an uncertain committed operation and announces recovery status.
Recovery preserves text, avoids duplicate revisions and restores usable focus; the next edit remains possible.
evidence: Input snapshots, operation/revision counts, announced state transitions and focus trace.

cases.title: Distinguish a first release from an upgrade claim

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: One release fixture has a recorded W predecessor and another is the initial W release with no predecessor; their release histories are retained.
steps: Request previous-release qualification evidence for both fixtures.
Inspect the evidence basis and capability report.
expectedOutcome: The successor requires an executed upgrade from its actual previous W release.
The initial release records predecessor absence and an explicit unexercised upgrade obligation; a fresh install cannot be labeled an upgrade pass.
evidence: Release-history basis and qualification reports for both predecessor states.

cases.title: Bind apply to the exact reviewed snapshot and destination version

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: A dry-run plan binds a package digest, renderer versions and destination version tokens; it includes one update and retains an omitted existing page.
steps: Apply an unchanged reviewed plan in one fixture.
In independent fixtures change one source byte after review, change one destination version, or change a renderer version before apply.
expectedOutcome: The unchanged plan applies once and retains the omitted page.
Every changed fixture reports a stale-plan conflict and requires a new dry run; no partial authoritative apply occurs.
evidence: Plan bindings, source/destination fingerprints, conflict diagnostics and retained-page comparison.

cases.title: Reject package incompatibility and identity collisions

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: A valid version-1 package and destination supply the control fixtures; existing destination content has an unbound route /guide.
steps: Independently use unsupported format version 2, an unsupported type schema version, an absent renderer and an unresolved reference.
Separately attempt to claim /guide and to redefine a type under its existing key/version with different field meaning.
expectedOutcome: Each dry run produces a specific version, dependency, reference or collision blocker.
No blocked plan mutates schemas, drafts, mappings, media metadata or publication; collisions never silently adopt or overwrite an object.
evidence: Six plan diagnostics and before/after authoritative inventories.

cases.title: Upgrade the actual previous website release

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: The previous supported W release is deployed with two types, three revisions per page, a blog post, two documentation versions, custom compatible renderer code, media, route redirects and stable import mappings. A coordinated backup and supported upgrade plan exist.
steps: Record both exact release identities and run preflight and the supported upgrade.
Read old and current publication fixtures, exercise the custom renderer and compare content, schema and mapping identities.
expectedOutcome: Upgrade preserves supported custom behavior, selected and historical content, media hashes and stable package mappings.
The target release reports the completed migration path and all incompatibilities explicitly.
evidence: Previous/target release identities, preflight/migration logs, before/after semantic snapshots and renderer journey results.

cases.title: Round-trip a package through reviewed import

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: A W site contains versioned types, selected revisions, media, taxonomy, navigation, redirects and two pinned documentation versions. A fresh destination has matching renderer versions and prequalified site binding.
steps: Export the selected content as a version-1 package and capture its digest.
Dry-run on the destination, review stable-key mappings, apply, then export the imported selection again.
Repeat the completed apply using its original operation identity.
expectedOutcome: Round-trip semantic content, fields, body order, references, routes and media hashes match; destination database ids may differ.
Repeated apply returns its recorded result without duplicate revisions or mappings, and import alone does not publish.
evidence: Both package digests, semantic comparison, reviewed plan, per-item outcomes and mapping/revision counts.

cases.title: Resume an import and recover from failed publication activation

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: A reviewed package updates two drafts and stages one media version. manifest-1 remains active and compatible; operation-1 identifies the reviewed plan.
steps: Interrupt once after media staging before database commit and, in a separate run, after database commit before acknowledgement.
Reconcile operation-1 before retrying and inspect per-item outcomes.
Attempt publication with a fault before activation commit, then recover using the retained validated manifest.
expectedOutcome: Uncommitted authoritative changes roll back; a committed apply returns its original result without duplication.
Staged media is accounted for and only unreferenced staging is cleaned. Failed activation preserves manifest-1 and its usable media/revisions.
evidence: Two checkpoint reports, mapping/revision counts, staging reconciliation, immutable manifest hashes and recovery result.

cases.title: Recover a failed application upgrade through its supported plan

scope.website: W previous-release upgrade and version-1 content-package portability, including stable mappings, dependencies, collisions, interruption and failed activation. First-release absence of a predecessor is recorded explicitly.

preconditions: The previous W release and its coordinated backup include custom content, stable mappings and historical media; the target upgrade has a documented forward-repair or restore path.
steps: Inject migration failure at its recorded checkpoint and retain the diagnosis.
Execute the supported recovery plan and read the restored or repaired application's published and historical content.
expectedOutcome: Recovery reaches a coherent supported application/schema pair with retained data and custom-content behavior.
Progress names the failed migration and repair outcome; no untested destructive reversal is assumed.
evidence: Exact release/backup identities, checkpoint and recovery records, content/mapping comparisons and restored application reads.

cases.title: Reconcile effects that straddle the backup boundary

scope.website: W coordinated restore of PostgreSQL, schemas, revisions, immutable manifests and filesystem Files into a recovery deployment prequalified by AC-004; derived cache rebuild and publication/email reconciliation only.

preconditions: The backup captures one scheduled publication and one queued contact email. After capture, publication activation and transport acceptance occur in the original deployment and their operation identities are retained.
steps: Restore the snapshot with execution held for reconciliation.
Compare schedule/publication and email identities with their postbackup outcomes before resuming.
Inspect each work item's disposition.
expectedOutcome: Already completed activation and accepted transport work are recognized under their original identities.
Uncertain outcomes remain explicit; resumption never blindly replays an external effect merely because the restored queue says pending.
evidence: Backup cutoff, postbackup outcome records, per-item reconciliation decisions and resumed-effect counts.

cases.title: Refuse an inconsistent backup set

scope.website: W coordinated restore of PostgreSQL, schemas, revisions, immutable manifests and filesystem Files into a recovery deployment prequalified by AC-004; derived cache rebuild and publication/email reconciliation only.

preconditions: A valid backup set is copied into two faulty fixtures: one omits a historically referenced file version and one combines a newer database snapshot with older Files.
steps: Restore and validate each fixture before declaring it ready.
expectedOutcome: Each restore reports the exact missing or mismatched reference and remains incomplete.
It cannot silently drop historical content or advertise successful readiness from a partial set.
evidence: Two backup inventories, failed reference/digest checks and readiness disposition.

cases.title: Restore authoritative website state and historical references

scope.website: W coordinated restore of PostgreSQL, schemas, revisions, immutable manifests and filesystem Files into a recovery deployment prequalified by AC-004; derived cache rebuild and publication/email reconciliation only.

preconditions: A coordinated backup includes type versions 1 and 2, current and historical revisions/manifests, media versions and their digest inventory. The recovery deployment and external-effect controls have been qualified separately.
steps: Restore PostgreSQL and Files from the same backup set.
Validate every manifest-to-revision-to-schema/renderer/media reference and read current and historical fixtures.
Rebuild derived delivery cache.
expectedOutcome: All restored authoritative identities and bytes match the coordinated inventory.
Current delivery selects the restored active manifest; historical versions remain resolvable, and derived cache agrees after rebuild.
