evidence: Backup-set identity, complete reference/integrity report, current/historical reads and rebuild results.

cases.title: Resume an interrupted restore without serving a mixed state

scope.website: W coordinated restore of PostgreSQL, schemas, revisions, immutable manifests and filesystem Files into a recovery deployment prequalified by AC-004; derived cache rebuild and publication/email reconciliation only.

preconditions: A complete backup and its expected digests are available. The restore can stop after database restore and midway through filesystem recovery.
steps: Interrupt at both checkpoints in independent runs.
Restart the restore, verify recovered objects and complete missing ones before rebuilding cache and declaring readiness.
expectedOutcome: Partial restores retain a visible incomplete state and never claim coherent delivery.
Repeated recovery verifies or restores each item without corrupting completed ones; final state matches the same backup set.
evidence: Checkpoint/progress records, per-object recovery results, digest comparison and final readiness/read observations.

cases.title: Rebuild derived state and resume reconciled schedules and email

scope.website: W coordinated restore of PostgreSQL, schemas, revisions, immutable manifests and filesystem Files into a recovery deployment prequalified by AC-004; derived cache rebuild and publication/email reconciliation only.

preconditions: Authoritative restore is complete; cache is stale, one publication is due, one email is known unsent and one has an unresolved transport outcome.
steps: Rebuild cache from the active manifest.
Apply the declared schedule misfire policy and dispatch only the known-unsent contact.
Resolve the uncertain transport identity before permitting its final disposition.
expectedOutcome: Cache converges without changing authoritative history; the due publication receives one recorded outcome.
Known-unsent work progresses once and ambiguous work stays visibly held until resolved, with no uncontrolled resend.
evidence: Cache generations, misfire decisions, email reconciliation records and effect counts after recovery.

cases.title: Measure the declared load and queue-capacity edges

scope.website: W small-site workload qualification for authoring, publish/delivery and coordinated restore on the declared single-host container tuple; security resource-abuse assurance remains AC-031 work.

preconditions: The supported fixture capacity is 20 concurrent readers, two authors and a 100-item publication-work queue; admission/backpressure semantics are recorded before measurement.
steps: Run reader loads of 19, 20 and 21 against the same dataset, recording the declared-capacity boundary.
Pause dispatch and submit 99, 100 and 101 distinct due work items in separate runs.
expectedOutcome: Results distinguish within-capacity measurements from overload; no evidence extends the release claim to unqualified load.
Queue outcomes match the declared capacity/backpressure contract, with each accepted item durable and every excess item explicitly handled.
evidence: Load/capacity matrix, latency/backlog series, admission outcomes and durable work counts.

cases.title: Expose resource pressure and a budget failure

scope.website: W small-site workload qualification for authoring, publish/delivery and coordinated restore on the declared single-host container tuple; security resource-abuse assurance remains AC-031 work.

preconditions: The same declared workload and budgets are retained. The test can delay filesystem reads enough to exceed the delivery budget while leaving data intact.
steps: Inject the recorded delay during the measured interval and continue authoring and publication.
Inspect latency, backlog, operation outcomes and the capability report.
expectedOutcome: The measured budget failure is reported with its fault conditions and cannot be summarized as a passing run.
Backlog and rejected/failed operations remain visible; no successful response conceals a lost committed save or publication.
evidence: Fault timing, raw latency/resource/backlog samples, operation reconciliation and failing budget verdict.

cases.title: Measure a declared small-site workload

scope.website: W small-site workload qualification for authoring, publish/delivery and coordinated restore on the declared single-host container tuple; security resource-abuse assurance remains AC-031 work.

preconditions: Use one site/culture, 100 pages with three revisions each, 20 blog posts, two documentation versions and 100 MiB of media. The release-approved budget sheet fixes numeric p95 authoring/delivery latency, publish-to-convergence time, error rate, peak memory and restore-time limits before the run. Hardware, runtime, container and provider versions are pinned.
steps: Warm up for five minutes, then run 20 concurrent readers and two authors for 15 minutes, each author saving once per minute and publishing every fifth save.
Restore the coordinated dataset into the qualified recovery fixture and time integrity verification and readiness.
expectedOutcome: Report each measured percentile, throughput, error count, resource peak, convergence delay and restore duration against its predeclared limit.
A pass requires all applicable budgets and content/integrity assertions to hold on this tuple; missing budget inputs prevent qualification.
evidence: Exact workload/budget sheet, hardware/version inventory, raw timed samples, resource series, restore digest report and per-budget verdicts.

cases.title: Measure recovery under the declared website workload

scope.website: W small-site workload qualification for authoring, publish/delivery and coordinated restore on the declared single-host container tuple; security resource-abuse assurance remains AC-031 work.

preconditions: The positive-case workload and budget sheet are fixed; a coordinated backup and a completed baseline measurement exist.
steps: During load restart the application after a committed publication and before cache convergence.
Reconcile queued work, rebuild cache and repeat the same measured interval.
Rehearse restore from the backup and compare time to readiness and data integrity with the declared recovery budget.
expectedOutcome: Committed work is retained and cache converges to the active publication.
Measurements expose outage and recovery duration as well as steady-state results; restore meets its declared budget and integrity checks or reports a specific qualification failure.
evidence: Restart and recovery timeline, operation/manifest comparison, repeated workload samples and timed restore integrity results.
